newsitem.title: UK: Gold recovers some losses, but market cautious.
newsitem.headline: Gold recovers some losses, but market cautious.

text.p: Gold prices recouped some strength on Wednesday, a day after sliding to 18-month lows.
Dealers saw possible further gains in the near term but cautioned that gold was eventually likely to retest recent lows and then drop further.
Explaining the price bounce amidst a month-old downtrend, a dealer said: "It's been too bearish to be true recently and when everyone's bearish, it tends to go the other way."
Gold closed at $380.60 an ounce in London, up from Tuesday's $378.65.

Dealers said the price was meeting stubborn resistance just above the key $380 an ounce level despite a bout of short covering which occurs when market expectations that prices will head lower reverse.
"There's a little bit of short covering...but I don't know how long-lived that's going to be," a dealer said.
Strength in the dollar and booming U.S. stock and bond markets are discouraging investor interest, while physical demand is on hold until prices bottom out, analysts said.
Poor Asian demand and the prospect of producer forward selling and central bank sales all pointed to a bear trend, said metals analyst Ted Arnold of broker Merrill Lynch.

"By the middle of September sentiment was clearly beginning to turn bearish and now I suspect it is only a matter of weeks before we see the $370 basis spot support level decisively broken on the downside," Arnold said.
After prices hit $370, an attempt towards $350 could not be ruled out, Arnold added.
Silver ended barely changed at $4.93, up two cents.
Prices had firmed from the high $4.80s on Tuesday afternoon on a shortcovering rally. But dealers said gains toward the key $5.00 resistance level would be hard won.
"Silver has been having lots of problems closing above $4.92. There's a lot of resistance below $5.00," one said.
Platinum was steady, ending just $0.50 above Tuesday's London close, at $384.75. On the upside it targeted $385.
Palladium closed at $121.00 an ounce, after breaking above its important $120 resistance level for the first time since it cracked over a week ago. Prices hit three-year lows last month.
